title: Tim J. Harris v. Heritage Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint not sustained. On Issue 1, the SJC answered No: the BCO has no explicit or implicit requirement that changes in a pastor's call be approved by congregational vote; after the original call, changes are budgetary and assigned to the Session under BCO 12-5b. On Issue 2, it answered No: no constitutional provision requires the Session to publicize the details of the budget, though the SJC counseled prudence and review upon inquiry. Heritage Presbytery's adoption of the CPC Commission report was left in effect; seven commissioners dissented.
first_summary: Harris complained that Heritage Presbytery erred in ruling the BCO did not require congregational approval of changes in a pastor's call and did not require publicizing budget details. The SJC held the BCO requires neither, so the complaint was not sustained. A dissent argued that congregational approval follows implicitly from the congregation's vows and the pastor's call.
summary: A church member challenged Heritage Presbytery's ruling that the BCO neither expressly nor implicitly requires a congregation to approve changes in a pastor's call, and that it does not require the session to publicize budget details. The SJC held the BCO silent on both points: once the original call and terms are approved, later changes are budgetary and belong to the session under BCO 12-5b; publicizing the budget is prudent but not mandated. The complaint was not sustained; seven commissioners dissented, arguing congregational approval follows by good and necessary consequence.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Source lines 1–5 identify case 2004-03, Tim J. Harris v. Heritage Presbytery, decided by the SJC at the 33rd General Assembly (2005), disposition not sustained, with dissent. Lines 103–111 report adoption: majority opinion by TE Dominic Aquila and RE Terry Jones; vote 14 concur, 7 dissent, 1 disqualified, 2 absent.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 13–31 and 33–37 describe Harris's complaints: first to the CPC Session seeking detailed public disclosure including salaries; then to Heritage Presbytery after the Session decided to publish a detailed budget but aggregate salaries; Heritage appointed a commission and adopted its report on January 31, 2004. The SJC issues were whether the BCO required congregational approval of changes in a pastor's call and whether it required publication of such changes or budget details.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 39–43 record the SJC's Judgment: both issues answered No. Lines 47–101 give the adopted reasoning: BCO 20-6 and 12-5b; no explicit or implicit requirement for congregational approval; later changes are budgetary and the Session's responsibility; the failed 1993 amendment and former PCUS practice are explained; no public-disclosure mandate is found, only prudential counsel to present and allow review of budget details. Lines 113–137 contain the non-adopted dissent.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 103–111 show the majority opinion as adopted, with seven named dissenters, one disqualified, and two absent. Lines 57–89 cite advisory statements from the 11th and 14th General Assemblies and the failed 21st General Assembly amendment as background and reasoning, not as binding constitutional mandates. The dissent's good-and-necessary-consequence argument is separate from the adopted holding.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate SJC decision is incorporated by reference. The challenged Heritage Presbytery action adopted the CPC Commission report (lines 25–31), which the SJC left in effect by not sustaining the complaint. Prior General Assembly advisory answers and the failed BCO 20-1 amendment are cited but not adopted as controlling.
